InductiveBias: Dynamic Intensity Isolation: Isolates purely dynamic acceleration/rotation energy of the arm, normalizing static orientation offsets (gravity) for optimal cross-subject generalization.
Skin-Impedance Normalization: Uses a geometric mean scale to compress high-amplitude muscle bursts, preventing physiological outliers and electrode-impedance variations from dominating.
Kinetic Dispersion Sensitivity: Tracks the kinetic energy dispersion of movements, with quadratic scaling providing high sensitivity to fine tremors or rapid load adjustments.
Static Orientation Tracking: On accelerometer channels, isolates the static projection of gravity (1g) to act as a direct proxy for arm posture and joint angles under load.
Time-Domain Mean Frequency: Serves as a robust and computationally light time-domain proxy for mean firing frequency without requiring spectral FFT/Welch transformations.
Stroke Bound Indicator: Captures the maximum stroke range of a physical motion wave, aiding temporal attention layers in identifying concentric/eccentric lifting bounds.
Movement Smoothness \& Fatigue: Represents rate of acceleration change; elevated jerk highlights sudden micro-corrections and tremors under load.
Lift Cadence: Locates the dominant rhythm of rigid body movement, reflecting how lift pace and tremors adapt to varying load weights.
Joint Effort \& Complexity: Measures cumulative waveform distance, serving as a stable, noise-robust proxy for muscle activation force and frequency.
Contraction Energy: Reflects the active muscle power; directly proportional to the constant force of muscle contraction under stationary Gaussian assumptions.
Work Volume: Standardizes absolute physical activity levels across all axis channels, making energy estimation robust to variable lift execution speeds.
Kinematic Asperity \& Spikes: Quantifies presence of sudden motion adjustments or sharp correction spikes against a smooth background lift profile.
Motor Unit Recruitment Shift: Monitors the spectral bandwidth of muscle activations, indicating shifts in fiber recruitment profiles (slow vs. fast twitch) under load.
Denoised Signal Energy: Accumulates frequency-domain Welch power, providing a robust variance estimate that filters out transient high-frequency channel noise.
Movement Asymmetry: Captures the asymmetry of the acceleration distribution to model differing concentric (lifting) vs. eccentric (lowering) motion profiles.
Muscle Fatigue Biomarker: Measures the first spectral moment; shifts toward lower frequencies track muscle fatigue and synchronization under persistent loads.
Amplitude-Invariant Rate: Counts the signal crossings of the zero line; serves as a pure frequency biomarker that is immune to electrode placement skin-impedance shifts.
Muscle Duty Cycle: Measures the percentage of active contraction duration above a sensor noise floor ($10^{-5}$ V), highlighting muscular tension timing.
Peak Transient Stress: Identifies the single absolute peak intensity or rapid motion catch achieved in a lifting window.
Structural Complexity: Amplitude-invariant count of slope direction changes, capturing raw high-frequency waveforms inflection details.
MUAP Counting: Measures frequency of consecutive steps exceeding the threshold ($10^{-5}$ V), tracking the active density of motor unit discharges.
